answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled audit confirms fraud. The audit must compare claims with independently verifiable evidence, not merely count votes, or a sybil swarm can endorse itself. Spawning identities therefore multiplies capital at risk without multiplying influence for free: an attacker must fund each stake and may lose it. A walnut shipment logged at a jetty and checked against a wharf receipt illustrates a claim an auditor can verify.
